Thirty minutes, Rehana. That's how long the group discussion round lasted, and for the first ten I didn't open my mouth. Twelve of us around a table for a campus placement. That evening I asked my roommate, who was in the same group, what she remembered about me. She said, "You made the rural banking point. It was good." That's all.

Rashmi sits two rows ahead of me in our pharmacy lectures. I'm Yash, and I've noticed something this semester. Whenever Dr Menon asks a question, Rashmi's hand half-lifts and then drops, and she writes the answer in the margin instead. She's usually right. I can see it from my seat.
In week two she did answer once, and stumbled over a long drug name. A couple of people smiled. By lunch, honestly, nobody was talking about it; everyone was complaining about the canteen queue.
But since then her hand hasn't gone up. I don't know what's going on in her head. Maybe she thinks we're all still thinking about that name. Maybe it's something else.
Today I leaned forward and said, "Your margin answer was right, you know." She looked surprised, then smiled a little.

qa.a: Yash seems to notice and care, maybe a little frustrated that right answers stay in the margin, which is why Yash finally leans forward to say something.

Week one, Monday. In the first sociology seminar at his Delhi college, Divyansh, nineteen, answered a question and called a famous thinker by the wrong name. Someone at the back chuckled. His ears burned all day.
Week three, Thursday. He hadn't spoken since. Twice he had a good point about the reading ready, his hand half lifted, and both times he put it down. They'll remember the name thing, he thought. They'll think I'm a fraud.
Week five, Tuesday. In the canteen, Mohit, who sat beside him in every seminar, said, "You barely talk in class. You okay?"
Divyansh blurted, "After I messed up that name?"
Mohit frowned. "What name?"
He genuinely had no idea. Divyansh sat there with his samosa going cold, thinking about five weeks of silence over something nobody else remembered.
